rationale: Interval-level: ensemble std correlates with teacher |error| (Spearman r=0.426, Pearson r=0.472) and Large |error| (Spearman r=0.435, Pearson r=0.455); bootstrap CIs exclude 0. Calibration across 10 equal-frequency bins is strongly monotonic (bin Spearman teacher=0.976, large=0.952). Type-level: disagreement strongly tracks type RMSE (Spearman vs teacher RMSE=0.757, vs Large RMSE=0.832) and is higher for rare/hard types (top: B744/B77W/B772). Top-vs-bottom disagreement types show mean student-gap delta = +49.35 kg. Type-level correlation with student gap itself is weak (Spearman r=0.136); disagreement marks difficulty more than the gap directly, which is still informative for adaptive beta(x).
type_level_note: Disagreement is a strong difficulty signal (error/RMSE) but only a weak linear predictor of the student-teacher gap across types; Adaptive KD should use it as a hardness prior, not as a direct gap estimator.
